methods.name: to_dict
methods.summary: Return the config as the JSON-ready dict `adapter_config.json` holds.
methods.extended:
Enums become their strings and sets of module names sorted lists,
so the result goes straight to `json.dumps` and back through
`from_dict`.  A field the reference's config of this method lacks
(`IA3Config.layers_to_transform`) is written only when it is set,
so a file that does not use it is one the reference reads too.

returns.description: One entry per field, keyed by the reference's field names.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> d = LoraConfig(target_modules=["v", "q"], task_type="CAUSAL_LM").to_dict()
>>> d["target_modules"], d["task_type"], d["peft_type"]
(['q', 'v'], 'CAUSAL_LM', 'LORA')

methods.name: from_dict
methods.summary: Build a config from a dict such as a parsed `adapter_config.json`.
methods.extended:
The constructor cannot do this: a file from the reference carries
keys v1 has no field for.  Such a key is accepted only at a value
that turns its feature off — null, false or empty
(`"loftq_config": {}`, `"megatron_config": null`) — and dropped (with
a warning if v1 does not know the key); at any other value it
raises, as it would change what the adapter computes.  The
`peft_version` provenance key is kept as the field it is.

The dict's `peft_type` picks the class, whichever class this is called
on, as the reference's `from_peft_type` does: `LoraConfig.from_dict` of
an OFT dict is an `OFTConfig`.  A dict that names no method is read as
the calling class (as LoRA on `PeftConfig`).

parameters.name: config_dict
parameters.description: The config's fields, by the reference's names.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class the dict's method names.

raises.description: `peft_type` names no method of this library.
The dict turns on a feature v1 lacks.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> config = LoraConfig.from_dict(
...     {"peft_type": "LORA", "r": 4, "target_modules": ["c_attn"],
...      "use_dora": False, "loftq_config": {}, "peft_version": "0.17.0"})
>>> config.r, config.target_modules
(4, {'c_attn'})
>>> type(LoraConfig.from_dict({"peft_type": "OFT", "target_modules": ["q"]})).__name__
'OFTConfig'

methods.name: save_pretrained
methods.summary: Write `adapter_config.json` into `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
The file is the reference's: `to_dict` with its keys sorted,
indented by two spaces.  The directory is created if missing.

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
`auto_mapping_dict` replaces the `auto_mapping` the file records.
The reference forwards any other keyword to its hub upload; there
is no hub here, so another key raises.

raises.description: `save_directory` names an existing file.
`kwargs` holds a key other than `auto_mapping_dict`.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["fc"]).save_pretrained(d)
...     LoraConfig.from_pretrained(d).r
2

methods.name: from_json_file
methods.summary: Read a config file into the dict it holds, unchanged but for `runtime_config`.
methods.extended:
What `from_pretrained` reads before it chooses a config class: the
file's content as a dict, as the reference's `from_json_file` returns
it.  `from_dict` turns it into a config.

parameters.name: path_json_file
parameters.description: The path of a JSON file such as `adapter_config.json`.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
Accepted for the reference's signature; it passes none to the
reader, and any key given here raises.

returns.description:
The file's object, without a `runtime_config` key: the
reference warns that such a key is ignored, since a runtime
configuration is valid at runtime only.

raises.description: There is no file at `path_json_file`.
The file does not hold a JSON object.
`kwargs` is not empty.

examples:
>>> import os, tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["fc"]).save_pretrained(d)
...     raw = PeftConfig.from_json_file(os.path.join(d, "adapter_config.json"))
>>> raw["peft_type"], raw["r"]
('LORA', 2)

methods.name: from_pretrained
methods.signature: from_pretrained(pretrained_model_name_or_path: str | os.PathLike[str], subfolder: str | None = None, kwargs: object = {})
methods.summary: Read `adapter_config.json` from a local adapter directory.
methods.extended:
The file's `peft_type` picks the config class, whichever class this is called
on (`PeftConfig.from_pretrained` of a LoRA adapter is a `LoraConfig`, and
`LoraConfig.from_pretrained` of an OFT adapter an `OFTConfig`), as the
reference's does.  The file's keys go through that class's `check_kwargs`
first, before any is dropped for being unknown, and then through `from_dict`.
The reference calls the `check_kwargs` of the class this is called on, which is
the file's class on the paths that load a model; here it is the file's class on
every path, so an OFT file is checked when read through `PeftConfig` too.

parameters.name: pretrained_model_name_or_path
parameters.description:
A directory holding `adapter_config.json` — one written by
`save_pretrained` or by the reference library.  Hub ids
are not resolved; download the adapter first.

parameters.name: subfolder
parameters.description:
A directory under `pretrained_model_name_or_path` that holds
the file, e.g. the sub-directory `save_pretrained` gives each
adapter but the one named `"default"`.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description:
The reference forwards these to its hub download (`revision`,
`token`, `cache_dir` …).  Adapters are read from a local
directory, so any key given here raises.

returns.description: The config, read through `from_dict`, of the class the file's `peft_type` names.

raises.description: The directory has no `adapter_config.json`.

The file does not hold a JSON object, or its class's `check_kwargs` refuses it
(an OFT file of the reference's before 0.14.0).
The file's `peft_type` names no method of this library.
`kwargs` is not empty, or the file turns on a feature this library lacks.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, target_modules="all-linear").save_pretrained(d)
...     loaded = LoraConfig.from_pretrained(d)
>>> loaded.r, loaded.lora_alpha, loaded.target_modules
(16, 32, 'all-linear')

warns.description:
The file's class's `check_kwargs` warns (an OFT file of the reference's before
0.18.0 that records its `peft_version`), or the file has a key this library has no
field for.

methods.name: from_peft_type
methods.summary: Build a config from its fields given as keyword arguments, the class chosen by `peft_type`.
methods.extended:
The reference's way to turn the keys of a config file into a config: the
`peft_type` argument names the method and so the class, whichever class this is
called on.  Without one, the calling class is built.  The fields are read as
`from_dict` reads them, so a key this library has no field for is accepted
at a value that turns its feature off (dropped, with a warning when the key is
unknown), where the reference drops it at any value.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description: The config's fields, by name; `peft_type` is a `PeftType` or its string.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class `peft_type` names.

raises.description: `peft_type` names no method of this library.
No `peft_type` is given and this is `PeftConfig` itself, which builds no config of its own.
A key turns on a feature this library does not implement.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftConfig
>>> config = PeftConfig.from_peft_type(peft_type="LORA", r=4, target_modules=["q"])
>>> type(config).__name__, config.r
('LoraConfig', 4)
>>> LoraConfig.from_peft_type(r=2, target_modules=["q"]).r
2

methods.name: check_kwargs
methods.summary: Check the fields about to build a config; the reference's hook for a class to refuse a file it cannot read.
methods.extended:
`from_pretrained` calls it on the keys of an adapter file, on the class the file
names and before any key is dropped for being unknown, as the reference does.
A config class overrides it to refuse or warn about a file written for an older
release of its method (`OFTConfig.check_kwargs`); the base accepts everything.
`from_dict` and `from_peft_type` do not call it.

parameters.name: **kwargs
parameters.description: The config's fields, by name.

returns.description: The fields to build the config with: `kwargs` itself.

members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a model with OSF.
members.extended:
OSF (Orthogonal Subspace Fine-tuning; Nayak et al., 2025, [arXiv:2504.07097](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07097) — Sculpting Subspaces, section 3)
is constrained full fine-tuning for continual learning.  It takes the SVD of each weight, freezes the top
`effective_rank` singular directions, which carry what the model already knows, and trains the rest, with
gradients projected orthogonally to the frozen directions so that a new task does not overwrite an old one.
The trainable rank is `min(weight.shape) - effective_rank`; no parameter is added to the model.

parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.PeftConfig`.

parameters.name: peft_type
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.PeftConfig`.

parameters.description:
Rank of the frozen high subspace.  An integer is a count; a float in `(0, 1]` is a
fraction of the smaller weight dimension; `None` takes half of it.

parameters.name: rank_pattern
parameters.annotation: dict of str to int or float
parameters.description:
Per-module overrides of `effective_rank`, keyed by regex; values are counts or
fractions.

parameters.name: init_weights
parameters.description:
`True`: the trainable components start from the weight's own decomposition, so the
adapter is the identity.  `False`: they start random (for tests).

parameters.name: target_svd_config
parameters.description: Per-parameter SVD ranks, by parameter name; accepted for compatibility and not used.

parameters.name: target_modules
parameters.description: The modules OSF adapts, matched as `LoraConfig.target_modules` is.

parameters.name: modules_to_save
parameters.description: As in `lucid.peft.LoraConfig`.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import OSFConfig
>>> config = OSFConfig(effective_rank=0.5, target_modules=['q_proj', 'v_proj'])
>>> sorted(config.target_modules), config.peft_type
(['q_proj', 'v_proj'], <PeftType.OSF: 'OSF'>)
>>> OSFConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config
True
notes:
Field names, their order, defaults and `adapter_config.json` are the reference library's.
`TypeError` is raised when a field holds a value of the wrong type.  A model type with no
default row (`gpt2` has one) adapts every linear layer when `target_modules` is left unset.

members.name: Linear
members.signature: Linear(base_layer: nn.Module, adapter_name: str, config: C)
members.summary: An `nn.Linear` whose low singular directions train: $y = (W + U\Sigma V^\top - U^0\Sigma^0 V^{0\top})\,x + b$.

parameters.name: base_layer
parameters.description: The layer to adapt; the other parameters are those of `OSFLayer`.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the first adapter.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: `effective_rank` (a count, a fraction of the smaller side, or `None` for half of it) and `init_weights`.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import OSFConfig
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.osf import Linear
>>> base = nn.Linear(8, 6)
>>> layer = Linear(base, "default", OSFConfig(effective_rank=2, target_modules=["x"]))
>>> {name: tuple(p.shape) for name, p in layer.osf_svd_params["default"].items()}
{'U_low': (6, 4), 'S_low': (4,), 'V_low': (4, 8)}
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 8)
>>> bool((layer(x) == base(x)).all().item())   # the trained part starts as the weight's own
True

The adapter is built whole before the layer holds any of it.  A layer
that holds an adapter already keeps applying the adapters it applied:
the new one is inactive until `set_adapter` names it; a layer with
none starts applying this one.

The names this layer holds nothing for are skipped by the forward
pass.  A merged layer is unmerged first, since the active adapters
are no longer the merged ones.

parameters.name: adapter_names

methods.name: merge
methods.signature: merge(safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Fold the update into the base weights, in place.
methods.extended:
The weights keep their identity — they are written, not replaced —
so whatever holds them (an optimizer, a tied embedding) sees the
merged values.  That is also why a weight shared with another
module must not be merged into; the tuner's `merge_adapter` and
`merge_and_unload` refuse it, as this layer alone cannot see the
rest of the model.

Merging some of the active adapters leaves the rest applying: the layer's
forward pass runs the folded weights and then the active adapters that are
not folded, so it computes what it did unmerged.  The reference runs a
merged layer's base alone, which drops the others — a deliberate departure
(LCD-971).  A method whose adapters would not compute the same function
that way (rotations that must apply in order, DoRA reading the weight)
refuses the split in the tuner's `merge_adapter`, before it writes
anything; this method, called on a layer directly, does not check it.
Merging an adapter that is not active adds it: the layer then runs the weights
with it folded in and the active adapters it has not folded (the base with that
adapter alone, in the reference).

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description:
Check the merged weights for NaN / inf first and leave the base
untouched if there are any.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: Adapters to merge; the active ones this layer holds by default.

raises.description:
An adapter name this layer does not hold, or `safe_merge`
found a non-finite merged weight.

The adapter is disabled, or the layer's own rules refuse the merge
(`lora_bias` on a base with no bias).
This layer's update cannot be written into its base weights.

methods.name: unmerge
methods.summary: Take every merged update back out of the base weights, in place.
methods.extended:
The result equals the original weights up to the rounding of the
round trip.

The base output alone when adapters are disabled or every active adapter is merged (a
merged adapter is in the base weights already); the sum is cast back to the base
output's dtype.

methods.name: unmerge_adapter
methods.summary: Take every merged adapter update back out of its base weight.
methods.extended:
The reference refuses to unmerge an OSF adapter and declares `(*args, **kwargs)`; here the
update is a plain difference added to the weight, so it can be taken out again, and the
signature stays the reference's.

raises.description: An argument is given: there is nothing to pass.

methods.name: active_adapters
methods.summary: The adapters the forward pass applies, as a list.

methods.name: add_adapter
methods.summary: Add an adapter beside the ones the model holds.
methods.extended:
The new adapter starts frozen and inactive: the forward pass keeps
applying the adapters it applied, and every parameter keeps the
`requires_grad` it had.  `set_adapter` switches to it.  A
module an earlier adapter already wraps takes the new one beside
it; any other target is wrapped.  The model is left as it was if
the adapter cannot be added.

Layers that hold merged adapters stay merged, bit for bit, and the
adapter starts from the weights as they were before the merge, as it
would on the unmerged model.  An initialisation that writes the base
weights (PiSSA, OLoRA, LoRA-GA) cannot be applied where adapters are
merged: `unmerge_adapter` first.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the new adapter; unique among the model's adapters.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how — the config class of this tuner's method.

raises.description:
The name is taken or malformed, the config is another
method's, no module matches it, it cannot sit beside the
adapters held (two adapters training biases), or its
initialisation writes the base weights of a layer that holds
merged adapters.
`config` is not an adapter config.

methods.name: inject_adapter
methods.signature: inject_adapter(model: nn.Module, adapter_name: str, autocast_adapter_dtype: bool = True, low_cpu_mem_usage: bool = False, state_dict: dict[str, Tensor] | None = None)
methods.summary: Build the layers of adapter `adapter_name` into `model`, from the config `peft_config` holds for it.
methods.extended:
The reference's spelling of what `add_adapter` does: the config is not an argument but
is read from `peft_config[adapter_name]`, which the caller has set.  The adapter is added
as `add_adapter` adds it (one path): beside the adapters held, frozen and inactive, with
merged layers left merged and the new adapter built from the weights as they were; a
failure leaves the model as it was and `peft_config[adapter_name]` as the caller set it.
On success `peft_config[adapter_name]` is the stored config (its default targets
spelled out), not the object the caller set.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to adapt; this tuner's own `model`.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter, with its config in `peft_config` and no layer of it in the model yet.

parameters.name: autocast_adapter_dtype
parameters.description:
The reference's option to keep a half-precision base's adapter in its own dtype;
`False` raises `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description:
The reference's option to build the adapter on the meta device; `True` raises
`NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: state_dict
parameters.description:
The reference's option to match targets against state-dict keys rather than the
model's modules; anything but `None` raises `NotImplementedError`.

raises.description:
`model` is not this tuner's model, `peft_config` has no entry for
`adapter_name`, the model already holds an adapter of that name, or the adapter
cannot be applied (as in `add_adapter`).
The config set is not a config of this tuner's method.

`autocast_adapter_dtype`, `low_cpu_mem_usage` or `state_dict` holds a value the
library cannot honour.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, LoraModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4), nn.Linear(4, 4))
>>> tuner = LoraModel(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]), "default")
>>> tuner.peft_config["two"] = LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["1"])
>>> tuner.inject_adapter(net, "two")
>>> sorted(tuner.targeted_module_names), tuner.active_adapters
(['0', '1'], ['default'])

methods.name: set_adapter
methods.signature: set_adapter(adapter_name: str | list[str], inference_mode: bool = False)
methods.summary: Apply the named adapter(s) in the forward pass, and train exactly those.
methods.extended:
Every other adapter is frozen; the activated ones train unless
`inference_mode`.  A merged layer is unmerged first.  Layers that
hold none of the named adapters run their base alone.  The
parameters `bias` makes trainable follow the adapter that asked
for them.

parameters.description: The adapter, or adapters, to apply.

parameters.name: inference_mode
parameters.description: Freeze the activated adapters too.

raises.description:
A name is not one of the model's adapters, or two named
adapters train the same `modules_to_save` module.

methods.name: set_requires_grad
methods.signature: set_requires_grad(adapter_names: str | Sequence[str], requires_grad: bool = True)
methods.summary: Enable or disable gradients on the parameters of the named adapter(s).

raises.description: A name is not one of the model's adapters.

methods.name: delete_adapter
methods.summary: Remove an adapter: its parameters, its config, its `modules_to_save` copies.
methods.extended:
If it was active, the adapters still active stay so; when none
remain the first of the others (by name) takes over, with a
warning, and trains.  Deleting the last adapter leaves the layers
in the model, applying nothing; `unload()` removes them.

raises.description: The adapter does not exist, or it is merged — unmerge first.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Call the adapted model; its adapter layers do their work inside the call.

methods.name: merge_adapter
methods.signature: merge_adapter(adapter_names: list[str] | None = None, safe_merge: bool = False)
methods.summary: Fold adapter updates into their base weights, keeping the adapter layers.
methods.extended:
A merged model runs at the base model's cost; `unmerge_adapter`
takes the updates out again.  Every refusal is made before any
weight is written: nothing is merged if a layer's base weight is
shared with another module (a tied LM head — merging would change
that module too) or if the adapter is disabled.

Merging some of the active adapters leaves the others applying: a merged
layer runs its folded weights and then the active adapters it has not
folded, so the model computes what it did unmerged.  The reference runs a
merged layer's base alone, which drops the others; Lucid departs from that
on purpose (LCD-971).  Merging an adapter that is not active adds it: the
layers then run the weights with it folded in and the active adapters they
have not folded (the base with that adapter alone, in the reference).  A
method whose adapters do not compute the same function once split refuses
it: those that apply in order (OFT, BOFT, HRA, RoAd's `road_2` and
`road_4`, MiSS / Bone's `bat`) take only the first of the active
adapters, in their order; a LoRA layer refuses to fold some adapters while
a DoRA one stays unmerged; LN tuning, which runs one adapter's copy at a
time, refuses to fold an active adapter while another is active.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description:
Adapters to merge; the active ones by default.  A layer holding
only some of them merges those.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description: Check every merged weight for NaN / inf before writing any.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module, or the adapter is
disabled (inside `disable_adapter()`).

A name is not one of the model's adapters, `safe_merge` found a
non-finite merged weight, or a layer's method cannot go on applying
the active adapters that stay unmerged.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> config = LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"], init_lora_weights=False)
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4)), config)
>>> peft.add_adapter("two", config)
>>> peft.base_model.set_adapter(["default", "two"])
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> both = peft(x)
>>> peft.base_model.merge_adapter(adapter_names=["default"])
>>> peft.base_model.model[0].merged_adapters
['default']
>>> bool(lucid.allclose(peft(x), both, atol=1e-5))   # "two" still applies
True

methods.name: merge_and_unload
methods.signature: merge_and_unload(progressbar: bool = False, safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Merge the adapters into the base weights and return the plain model.
methods.extended:
Each adapter layer is replaced by its merged base module — the base
model's own module, holding its own `Parameter` objects — and each
`modules_to_save` entry by the active adapter's trained copy (the
original when that adapter has none).  Adapters not merged are
dropped with their layers.  Every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

parameters.name: progressbar
parameters.description: Accepted for the reference's signature; there is no progress bar.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description: Check every merged weight for NaN / inf before writing any.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: Adapters to merge; the active ones by default.

returns.description: The model, merged, with no adapter layer left in it.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module, or a
`modules_to_save` module shared one (its trained copy would
break the tie).

methods.name: unload
methods.summary: Remove every adapter without merging and return the original model.
methods.extended:
Every adapter layer is replaced by the module it wrapped (a merged
one is unmerged first), every `modules_to_save` entry by its
original module, and every base parameter gets back the
`requires_grad` it had before injection.

methods.name: enable_adapter_layers
methods.summary: Apply the adapter again after `disable_adapter_layers`.

methods.name: disable_adapter_layers
methods.summary: Run the base model alone: adapter updates off, original `modules_to_save`.

methods.name: supports_lora_conversion
methods.summary: Whether every adapted layer in this tuner supports conversion to LoRA.

methods.name: get_model_config
methods.summary: `model`'s config as a dict, whatever it is held as.
methods.extended:
A config with a `to_dict` method is converted by it, a dataclass by `asdict`, a
mapping is copied.  A model with no `config` (or one that is `None`) has the
reference's stand-in, `{"model_type": "custom"}`, which is what the default target
modules and the prompt geometry read for a model of no known type.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to read the config of.

returns.description: The config's entries; a new dict, whose changes do not reach the model.

raises.description: `model.config` is none of a mapping, a dataclass or an object with `to_dict`.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraModel
>>> LoraModel.get_model_config(nn.Linear(2, 2))
{'model_type': 'custom'}

members.summary: A network whose weights train in their low singular directions, with the gradients kept off the high ones.
members.extended:
Each `nn.Linear` that `config` selects is replaced by a `lucid.peft.tuners.osf.Linear`
that splits its weight by SVD, freezes the top `effective_rank` triplets and trains the rest,
its gradients projected onto the complement of the frozen directions; the number of frozen
triplets is the config's unless `rank_pattern` names the module.  Nothing is added to the network
beyond the split's own tensors.  The network is edited in place and stays reachable as `model`.
Adapters added later (`add_adapter`, `set_adapter`, `delete_adapter`) coexist, and the active
ones add their updates to the weight.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The network whose layers are split.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description:
The frozen rank, its per-module overrides and which modules.  Named `config`, not
`peft_config`, as in the reference.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: What the first adapter is called: the key of its `osf_svd_params` entry in every layer.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description:
Options of the reference that this library cannot honour: anything but the default raises,
as in `lucid.peft.LoraModel`.

parameters.name: state_dict
parameters.description:
Options of the reference that this library cannot honour: anything but the default raises,
as in `lucid.peft.LoraModel`.

raises.description:
Nothing matches `target_modules`; a match is not an `nn.Linear`; the frozen rank comes out
as zero; or `modules_to_save` matches nothing.
The network already carries layers of another method.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import OSFConfig, OSFModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 8), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(8, 2))
>>> osf = OSFModel(net, OSFConfig(effective_rank=2, target_modules=["0"]), "default")
>>> osf.targeted_module_names
['0']
>>> net[0].base_layer.weight.requires_grad, net[0].osf_svd_params["default"]["U_low"].requires_grad
(False, True)
>>> osf.unload() is net, type(net[0]) is nn.Linear
(True, True)

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.osf` — OSF: constrained full fine-tuning in the weight's low singular directions.
extended:
OSF (Nayak et al., 2025, [arXiv:2504.07097](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07097) — Sculpting Subspaces) takes the SVD of each weight,
freezes its top singular directions, which carry what the model already knows, and trains the rest, with
the gradients projected onto the complement of the frozen directions so that a new task does not overwrite
an old one.  Nothing is added to the model: the trained tensors are the weight's own low part.  Pick it for
learning several tasks in sequence without keeping an adapter per task.

Where the reference library keeps them, so `isinstance(m, OSFLayer)` and `from
lucid.peft.tuners.osf import OSFConfig, Linear` read as they do there.  One layer type for the one
module the method adapts, `nn.Linear`.  `OSFConfig` and `OSFModel` are here and exported from
`lucid.peft`.  Importing the package registers the method (its config under `PeftType.OSF`, its
tuner and layer), which is what makes `get_peft_model` and `PeftModel.from_pretrained` know it.
citation: Nayak, Nikhil Shivakumar, et al. "Sculpting Subspaces: Constrained Full Fine-Tuning in LLMs for Continual Learning." [arXiv:2504.07097](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07097), 2025.
theory:
OSF (Orthogonal Subspace Fine-tuning; Nayak et al., 2025, [arXiv:2504.07097](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07097) — Sculpting Subspaces, section 3)
is constrained full fine-tuning for continual learning.  It takes the SVD of each weight, freezes the top
`effective_rank` singular directions, which carry what the model already knows, and trains the rest, with
gradients projected orthogonally to the frozen directions so that a new task does not overwrite an old one.
The trainable rank is `min(weight.shape) - effective_rank`; no parameter is added to the model.
